topic: Personas, Empathy Maps, and User Needs
learningObjectives: Create a basic persona from user research findings.
Identify what users say, think, feel, and do using an empathy map.
Convert research observations into actionable user needs.

activities.title: Persona Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore the key parts of a UX persona.

content.concept: A persona is a research-based representation of a meaningful user group. It commonly includes context, goals, behaviors, needs, frustrations, and motivations.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Provides a memorable representation without pretending to describe one specific real person.
Describes relevant background, situation, environment, or constraints.
Explains what the user wants to accomplish.
Captures patterns in what the user commonly does.
Identifies recurring frustrations or obstacles supported by research.
Describes what helps the user succeed and what motivates their behavior.

activities.title: Persona Builder
activities.instruction: Build a research-grounded persona using the essential components.

content.concept: A useful persona connects research evidence to a coherent user profile. Avoid adding unsupported demographics or assumptions simply to make the persona look detailed.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Empathy Map Explorer
activities.instruction: Explore the four main sections of an empathy map.

content.concept: Empathy maps help organize research around what users say, think, do, and feel. They help teams identify patterns rather than relying on isolated assumptions.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Direct statements or words expressed by the user.
Beliefs, concerns, questions, or thoughts inferred carefully from research evidence.
Emotions or feelings indicated by the user's words, behavior, or research evidence.

activities.title: Need vs Assumption
activities.instruction: Choose the statement that is supported by user evidence.

content.concept: A user need should describe something the user requires to achieve a goal. It should be grounded in research rather than an unsupported assumption about what users want.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

choices: Users need clear delivery-cost information before confirming an order.
Users probably want the website to have more animations.
config.answer: Users need clear delivery-cost information before confirming an order.
